Users prefer a common interface to an integrated interface in an experimental environment, and they prefer to have more control in their interaction with the system.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the user interface for distributed databases and the user preference for integrated or common interfaces.
how to support effective user interaction with distributed and heterogeneous digital libraries.
the design and implementation of a distributed digital library environment that allows for user choice of interaction with heterogeneous information resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the users prefer to interact with heterogeneous and distributed databases through a common user interface.
the users prefer a common interface to the integrated interface.
users are not satisfied with the existing integrated systems and would prefer a more flexible approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the users' preference for the integrated interaction is not as clear-cut as the IR literature has assumed.
the user preference is not a simple function of the number of databases involved, but a function of the characteristics of the databases and the interaction style.
the distributed IR environment is more complex than the traditional IR environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of digital library systems should allow for more user choice in terms of interaction with multiple databases.
the user preferences for integrated and common interfaces depend on how the user is allowed to interact with the interface.
the digital library environment is not a homogeneous space, and the users' preference for the interaction with multiple databases depends on the type of database, the user profile, and the task.
